knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly lists in order the post-fit moves after fitting a linear model in software?
knowledge_checks.body: Select fit, slope inference, prediction limits, residual check.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The chain is fit, slope inference, prediction with limits, residual checks. Skipping inference or residuals after fit is menu tourism.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Fit, slope inference, prediction with limits, residual checks for suitability.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Stopping at fitted coefficients without prediction limits or residual checks.

choices.label: Fit the model in software, then check slope inference (estimate, standard error, test or confidence interval), then use prediction with confidence or prediction limits, then inspect residuals to check suitability and validity of the linear model.
Fit the model, then run variable selection, then declare the model valid without residual checks because R-squared is displayed.
Fit the model and read the slope sign only; prediction limits and residual checks belong to GLM diagnostics, not linear regression.
Inspect residuals first, then fit the model, then skip slope inference because significance is automatic from the fit command.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.1.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. After fitting Y = β₀ + β₁ x in software you see β̂₁, SE(β̂₁), R-squared, and residual plots. For a new x-star, which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Distinguish mean versus individual prediction; refuse selection.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Mean interval targets the conditional mean; prediction adds observation noise. Fit-only and optional residuals are misconceptions.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Mean interval for E[Y | x*]; prediction wider; refuse fit-only and optional residuals.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting fit as finishing inference, or treating residuals as optional after significance.

choices.label: A mean-response interval covers E[Y | x*]; a prediction interval covers a new observation and is typically wider (adds residual variance). Fit alone is not enough: slope inference, goodness-of-fit, prediction limits, and residual checks are all required before trusting the fit.
I fitted the model so I am done; residual plots are optional after a significant slope.
Because the slope is significant, residual plots are optional diagnostic theatre.
The mean-response interval and prediction interval for x-star are the same width because both estimate E[Y | x-star] only.
